questions.subject: Biology
questions.prompt: Q1 (spoken answer). Explain codominance with the ABO blood group example.
questions.expected_answer: In codominance both alleles of a heterozygote are fully expressed, with no blending. In the ABO system the alleles I^A and I^B are codominant (both dominant over i), so a person with genotype I^A I^B has blood group AB and carries both A and B antigens on the red cells.

marking_scheme.criterion: Defines codominance: both alleles of a heterozygote are fully expressed
Gives the ABO example: blood group AB carries both A and B antigens on the red cells
States there is no blending or intermediate phenotype (unlike incomplete dominance)
Uses the allele notation: I^A and I^B are codominant, both dominant over i
